title: Abinadi teaches of the coming judgment
summary: After speaking, Abinadi stretches forth his hand and teaches that all people will see the Lord's salvation and confess God's just judgments. He says the wicked will be cast out.

explicit_facts.text: After Abinadi had spoken, he stretched forth his hand and said these words.
Abinadi teaches that every nation, kindred, tongue, and people will see the Lord's salvation and confess before God that his judgments are just.
He teaches that the wicked will be cast out and have cause to howl, weep, wail, and gnash their teeth because they would not hearken to the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi is present, speaking and gesturing with an outstretched hand.
unspecified_visual_details: Abinadi's appearance and the setting are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: The time shall come when all shall see the salvation of the Lord;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: when every nation, kindred, tongue, and people shall see eye to eye
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: and shall confess before God that his judgments are just.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: And then shall the wicked be cast out,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: and they shall have cause to howl, and weep, and wail, and gnash their teeth;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future judgment is taught, not shown as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the wicked or future judgment as physically present.

title: Mankind's fallen state
summary: Abinadi teaches that mankind became carnal and fallen, and that those who persist in sin and rebellion remain in that state.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi teaches that the devil beguiled the first parents, causing their fall and mankind to become carnal.
All mankind were lost, but God redeemed his people from their lost and fallen state.
One who persists in carnal nature, sin, and rebellion remains fallen and an enemy to God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi continues speaking in the same unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The first parents and the devil are mentioned in teaching, not described as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: For they are carnal and devilish,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: Thus all mankind were lost;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: But remember that he that persists in his own carnal nature,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: and goes on in the ways of sin and rebellion against God,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fall and redemption are teachings, not events to stage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the first parents, the devil, or a visual allegory of the fall.

title: Redemption and resurrection through Christ
summary: Abinadi teaches that redemption depends on Christ's coming and resurrection. He declares that Christ is the light and life of the world.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi teaches that without Christ's coming there could be no redemption.
He teaches that without Christ's rising from the dead there could be no resurrection.
He teaches that there is a resurrection, the grave has no victory, and death's sting is swallowed up in Christ.
Abinadi declares Christ to be the light and life of the world, endless and never darkened, with endless life and no more death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi continues speaking in the same unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Christ is discussed in the teaching but is not described as visibly present.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now if Christ had not come into the world,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: there could have been no redemption.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: And if Christ had not risen from the dead,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: there could have been no resurrection.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: But there is a resurrection,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: He is the light and the life of the world;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Christ's coming, resurrection, and victory over death are teachings here, not newly narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a resurrection scene, a grave, a visibly luminous Christ, or symbolic supernatural imagery.

title: Judgment according to works
summary: Abinadi teaches that mortals will put on immortality and stand before God's bar to be judged according to their works. He describes different outcomes for good and evil.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi teaches that mortals will put on immortality and the corruptible will put on incorruption, and that they will stand before God's bar to be judged according to their works.
He teaches that the good will rise to endless life and happiness, while the evil will rise to endless damnation.
He says the condemned followed their carnal wills and desires, did not call upon the Lord or depart from iniquities, and would not repent despite warnings and commands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi continues the sermon in the same unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: God's bar and the judgment outcomes are described as future doctrine, not a visible event in this scene.

spoken_dialogue.text: Even this mortal shall put on immortality,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: and this corruption shall put on incorruption,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: If they be good, to the resurrection of endless life and happiness;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: and if they be evil, to the resurrection of endless damnation,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Judgment and resurrection are future teachings; do not depict a heavenly courtroom.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show God, the devil, resurrected bodies, judgment proceedings, or invented sinners.

title: Repent and teach redemption through Christ
summary: Abinadi urges his listeners to repent and remember that salvation comes through Christ. He instructs them to teach that the law of Moses is a shadow of things to come and concludes with “Amen.”

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi urges his listeners to tremble, repent, and remember that they can be saved only through Christ.
He instructs them, if they teach the law of Moses, to also teach that it is a shadow of things to come.
He teaches that redemption comes through Christ the Lord, whom he calls the very Eternal Father, and concludes, “Amen.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi continues speaking in the same unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The listeners' presence, number, identities, and appearance are unspecified. No teaching object is mentioned.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now, ought ye not to tremble and repent of your sins,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: and remember that only in and through Christ ye can be saved?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: Therefore, if ye teach the law of Moses,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: also teach that it is a shadow of those things which are to come—
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: Teach them that redemption cometh through Christ the Lord,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: who is the very Eternal Father.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: Amen.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is the chapter's concluding exhortation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not make listeners visible or depict Christ or a law-of-Moses object.
